section.p: Lead/senior full-stack developerFull-stack developerfor the following websites: bymycar, maximiles.com, arturia.com, meinungsplatz.ch, madeindesign.com, deguisetoi.fr, kelkoo.com:

li.p: contributions on around forty e-commerce, loyalty, and panel (online surveys) websites, for the company and its clients/subsidiaries (white-label);

for the Bymycar and Bilendi websites (Maximiles, Meinungsplatz…), their multi-country FrontOffice/BackOffice are based on a component-oriented PHP/Symfony architecture: shared, customizable, and internationalized (100 bundles);

Bymycar uses a microservices architecture: REST API for importing vehicles from the ERP into the site, webhook for sending leads generated by the site into Salesforce, then sales opportunities generated by Salesforce into a dealership sales solution…;

development of a PoC using the new Ballerina technology: a “data-centric” and “cloud-native” language targeting integration scenarios between applications, microservice architectures and data processing;

types of sites: Bymycar (e-commerce), Banque Populaires/Bred (loyalty / cashback), UGC cinemas (offer and loyalty-card management), De Dietrich thermique (partner-installer loyalty), Meinungsplatz/Ivox/Club Nuove Idee (panel website), …;

contributions on various modules configurable per site: product catalog and partner feed management, promotions/campaigns, customer support, business monitoring (query/report configuration), online payments (World Pay, System Pay), bank transfers (protocol EBICS via partner Exalog), ERP stock and invoicing processes, print-on-demand…;
study and prototypes for migrating Arturia’s web shop based on Drupal/Symfony;
contributions on classic Web CMS modules (relational article model) and Structured CMS modules;
contributions on CMS modules:

evolving maintenance of classic CMS modules: relational model of articles/static content, with columns containing HTML fragments managed by marketing teams, and other columns locating content placement in website pages…;
addition of dynamic content management using Structured CMS design; the principle:
content types (without HTML) are defined by a JSON schema, content being edited with a schema-driven editor;
this content is then processed by a Symfony Content Aggregator Service, applying business rules instantiating dynamic parts of the content;
the final content is processed by a Twig macro structure generating the final front-end components;
migrations of Symfony 3/4, PHP 5/7 websites to Symfony 5/6, PHP 7/8;
management of translations/integration with Design/Marketing teams and front-end development: Bootstrap, Devextreme and jQuery frameworks;

section.p: Development tools used: (depending on the language) Phpstorm, Intellij IDEA, PyCharm (intensive use of the debugger).
Development practices used: mainly inspired by the following methodologies: TDD, Scrum, User Story Mapping, CMMI.
XP, CMMI, Scrum, User Story Mapping… all methodologies are good sources of inspiration, but none applies perfectly in all situations.
Here are the practices that worked best in my lead activity:

li.p: analyze requests and define the list of iteration 2 with requesters/product owner, in parallel with development of iteration 1;
define the to-do lists for resolving iteration-2 requests, which will be completed/adjusted during its development;
set up coaching/review for junior developers (on the solution/platform) by senior developers;

organize and manage regular “dev meetings,” during which topics owned by the team are discussed, debated, argued and collectively decided: technical architecture choices, implementation guidelines, demos, and any other topic someone wants to raise;
in short, help the team develop its own collective experience to address the challenges it faces ⇒ this is what endures over the long term;
… and after all these years co-developing in so many teams, I can make this statistical observation: developers who have integrated TDD reflexes and a debugger into their practice generally have
a better production non-regression rate,
more ability to reverse-engineer complex code (including legacy code), resolve complex bugs, and upskill on integrated packages/frameworks.
